items.title: Hashless venue guards let outsiders block new opens
items.description: An outsider can extend a growable venue without a stored ELF fingerprint, then block new opens until Emergency revalidation.

1.evidence: Accounts first: FlagVenueUpgraded:50-67 requires the canonical AccountLoader VenueGuard PDA/version, a venue index below VENUE_PROGRAMS, the compiled ProgramData key and loader owner; read_deploy_slot also requires its ProgramData header. Real CPMM ProgramData passes; there is no trusted signer. Local loader 4.2.2:793-794 and 4.3.0:789-790 dispatch legacy ExtendProgram with check_authority=false. Both require matching writable Program/ProgramData, loader ownership, a positive permitted increase, an upgradeable authority field, a later slot and rent funding; an outsider can supply these without the upgrade authority signature. Both resize, redeploy the unchanged ELF and store clock_slot. With guard_slot[4]=100, upgraded=0, guard_len[2]=0 and a successful extension in slot 101, flag_venue_upgraded:128 passes and :130-135 skips is_upgrade because VenueGuard::elf_fingerprint:110-114 returns None; :136 sets bit 4. Ordinary init/revalidation and downstream guards are traced below, not bypassed.

2.evidence: Source-reachable but deployment-conditional: InitializeConfig requires the real short.win upgrade-authority signer and new canonical accounts; an honest init writes upgraded=0 and guard_slot at :156-160 while leaving all fingerprint lengths zero. The enabled-venue bitmask permits CPMM. RevalidateVenue requires the configured pause-authority signer, canonical config/guard and authentic ProgramData; at the current expected_slot it accepts expected_elf_hash=[0;32], clears the fingerprint and clears the latch (:72-108). Neither path requires malicious governance. The outsider extension additionally requires a still-upgradeable account below the 10 MiB cap and a compatible active loader. Use 10,240 bytes when available, or the permitted smaller final increase to the cap. Immutable/full-sized accounts block this path; source-described capped Pump/PumpSwap accounts are excluded. No live fingerprint, size, authority or feature-state query was performed; source comments identifying growable venues are not live deployment validation.

3.evidence: The outsider pays any extension rent shortfall and transaction fees, then sends flag_venue_upgraded with authentic accounts. The matching account/address and payer signature requirements do not require the venue upgrade signer or the short.win Emergency signer. Honest init creates the condition directly, so this is an unprivileged amplifier of an ordinary initialization state, not harm caused solely by a malicious admin.

4.evidence: For an otherwise eligible existing Raydium market, open_short:291 calls guard::latch, whose :110-115 rejects the set bit before the trade. GUARD_MASK_RAYDIUM contains both Raydium bits, so either Raydium open is refused. The actual borrower signer, canonical config/guard/market, linked mint/vault/trader and usual prologue checks can all be satisfied by an honest caller; they do not clear the latch. create_market:553 also checks this Raydium mask; propose_pool:240 uses candidate_latch and blocks the flagged candidate program; execute_pool_switch:208 treats a flagged candidate as inadmissible. This interruption persists beyond the extension slot until Emergency revalidation. Existing exits, add_margin and withdrawals do not consult this latch; no existing funds lock or attacker profit is proved. The static complete conditional path scores 100 - 15 bounded/recoverable interruption - 10 specific hashless, still-growable state = 75. No runtime execution is claimed.

items.known_issue_comparison: Exact repeat of accepted KI-69(a), AIR-01 residual, and the pass-1 key shortwin|flag-venue-upgraded|unhashed-slot-upgrade-latch. KI-69 explicitly records initialization without fingerprints, hashless revalidation and permissionless extensions that latch venues. The runbook requires hashed bootstrap revalidations, but that procedure is not an on-chain guard. The initial ledger label NEW did not mean project-new. This is separate from AIR2-07 prefix collisions and KI-73 one-slot loader unavailability.

project_evidence.reason: KI-69 residual (a) expressly says initialize_config records no fingerprint, revalidation without a hash leaves none, and a permissionless extension then latches the venue until Emergency revalidation. The if-let fingerprint branch in flag_venue_upgraded is the same fallthrough. This is separate from AIR2-07 chosen-pair collisions and KI-73 loader one-slot unavailability.

source_evidence.root_cause: A growable venue can have an unflagged guard without an ELF fingerprint, so any changed ProgramData slot can set its upgrade latch.
source_evidence.guard_gap: flag_venue_upgraded checks is_upgrade only when elf_fingerprint returns Some; initialize_config leaves guard_len zero, and hashless revalidate_venue clears it again.
source_evidence.path: Initialize an enabled growable venue without its fingerprint, or clear its fingerprint through an honest revalidation -> an outsider pays to extend ProgramData -> flag_venue_upgraded sets the venue bit -> open_short refuses VenueUpgraded until Emergency revalidation.
source_evidence.proof: Use Raydium CPMM, venue=4, guard_slot[4]=100, upgraded=0, guard_len[2]=0, and an upgradeable ProgramData with at least 10,240 bytes below the 10 MiB size cap. At a later slot 101, the outsider submits the legacy loader ExtendProgram instruction with additional_bytes=10240 and its own payer. Local solana-bpf-loader-program-4.3.0/src/lib.rs:789-790 calls common_extend_program(..., false); lines 923-934 check the upgrade authority only when check_authority is true. Lines 968-971 resize the account, and lines 987-991 write slot=clock_slot. The outsider then passes the real CPMM ProgramData and canonical VenueGuard to flag_venue_upgraded(4). The owner/address/header checks pass; slot 101 differs from guard_slot 100. elf_fingerprint(4) returns None because guard_len[2]=0, so lines 130-135 skip is_upgrade and line 136 sets bit 4. GUARD_MASK_RAYDIUM at constants.rs:146 contains bits 3 and 4, and engine/guard.rs:113-119 rejects either Raydium open while either bit is set. Initialization reaches this state directly; revalidate_venue with expected_slot=current and expected_elf_hash=[0;32] also clears the fingerprint and latch. No venue upgrade signer is needed. The trace assumes the growable ProgramData state identified by this source; no live deployment size was queried. No build, test, or runtime reproduction was run.
source_evidence.guards: The fixed ProgramData address, loader owner, and tag prevent fake accounts. A recorded fingerprint rejects an unchanged ELF extension. Exits remain available.
source_evidence.impact: An outsider blocks new opens and candidate proposals for the extension rent and transaction fees; Emergency revalidation must restore the venue.
source_evidence.fix_notes: The patch covers new deployments. Existing deployments also need their growable venues revalidated with hashes before rollout. The proposed patch was not compiled.

source_evidence.boundary: flag_venue_upgraded's authentic ProgramData input and its hashless VenueGuard entry.
source_evidence.missing_check: identity of the reviewed executable after an externally authorized ProgramData extension.
source_evidence.assumption: A changed ProgramData slot proves an upgrade when no ELF fingerprint exists.
source_evidence.actual: An outsider can extend an upgradeable program without its authority signature and change the slot without changing the trimmed ELF.
source_evidence.path: Initialize a growable venue with guard_len = 0; extend its authentic ProgramData in a later slot; call flag_venue_upgraded; open_short fails with VenueUpgraded.
source_evidence.proof: Use the CPMM guard index 4 with upgraded = 0, guard_slot[4] = 100, guard_len[2] = 0, and an upgradeable ProgramData shorter than 10 MiB. In slot 101, send loader ExtendProgram with additional_bytes = 10,240, the authentic ProgramData and Program accounts writable, System, and an attacker payer. The pinned solana-bpf-loader-program 4.2.2 dispatches ExtendProgram to common_extend_program(..., false) at lines 793-794. Its authority check only runs when check_authority is true in common_extend_program. It preserves the authority and stores slot = clock_slot at lines 993-996. Then call flag_venue_upgraded(4) with the canonical guard and compile-time CPMM ProgramData key. The address, loader owner, and tag checks pass. slot != guard_slot passes. elf_fingerprint returns None because guard_len[2] is zero, so the handler skips is_upgrade and sets upgraded |= 16. The open guard rejects every venue whose mask includes this bit. initialize_config leaves all guard_len entries zero and upgraded = 0. revalidate_venue accepts an all-zero expected_elf_hash at the current slot and can restore the same vulnerable state.
source_evidence.guards_and_limits: The venue must remain upgradeable and have at least 10,240 bytes of headroom, or the caller must use the permitted smaller final extension. The caller pays any required rent. An immutable or full-sized ProgramData blocks the extension. A nonzero, correct stored fingerprint detects this unchanged ELF. Exits do not consult the latch. This is a static proof against the repository's pinned loader source; no live feature state or deployment was tested.
source_evidence.impact: An outsider blocks new opens and affected pool selection until Emergency revalidation records a fingerprint.
source_evidence.minimal_diff: This proposed startup fix changes no account layout. Existing deployments with empty fingerprints need an explicit bootstrap migration before reopening.

notes: Static source review only; present deployment exposure remains unverified. The account must remain upgradeable and have extension headroom.

Option A sets the four fingerprint-capable latch bits at initialization and rejects hashless revalidation. It retains the existing documented exact-slot trust in the supplied nonzero hash; that separate fail-safe residual is not this cause.

Option B iterates elf_index to set the same initialization bits and additionally verifies the full supplied hash even at an unchanged slot. With a changed slot, the new verification and the existing branch both hash the ELF. This adds compute cost and can exceed a budget that supports only one hash; no compute execution was performed.

Both options cover new initialization and future hashless revalidation, but neither migrates an existing unflagged guard with empty fingerprints. Existing deployments need an explicit hashed bootstrap before reopening.
No source edit, build, test, runtime reproduction, live interaction or git apply check was performed. The raw patches are proposals, not verified fixes.

fixes.label: Option A — Require hashes before enabling fingerprint-capable venues; existing guards need bootstrap
Option B — Require and verify hashes; repeats hashing after a slot change and needs bootstrap

items.title: Existing Pump UVAs skip full validation at listing
items.description: Listing accepts existing UVAs without decoding their user. A future venue layout can pass listing but fail trading; no current wrong-user path is proved.

1.evidence: create_market derives the UVA from the canonical trader PDA and the creator signs as payer; both init_uva helpers require the exact executable Pump/PumpSwap program, the derived UVA key and fixed event authority. Their existing-account branches at pump_amm:1161-1162 and pump_curve:1047-1048 require the venue owner and nonempty data but omit the discriminator, layout and user checks. Current trading parses those fields and requires the trader user (pump_amm::uva_ok:469-477; pump_curve::check_uva:766-779). The Solana owner/write rule and venue PDA derivation prevent an outsider from simply inserting wrong-user bytes at this canonical key. No present venue instruction or malicious state that bypasses this identity barrier was demonstrated. Retain the explicit hardening lead and stop before later gates.

project_evidence.reason: The original venue report specifically identifies both init_uva implementations skipping CPI for a nonempty venue-owned canonical UVA without decoding/user checks, despite stricter trade-time validation. The same branch remains in pump_curve::init_uva. The candidate is a prior raw hardening lead with a future venue-layout precondition, not a new project mechanism.

The existing-account branch then checks only the owner and nonempty data. The trading paths decode the UVA and require its user to equal the trader. The current venue PDA rules prevent outsiders from populating a different account type or user there. No current wrong-user creation path was proved.

source_evidence.boundary: The existing UVA branch of each create_market CPI helper.
source_evidence.proof: Neither existing-account branch checks the UVA discriminator, minimum layout, or stored user. Both return Ok immediately. The PumpSwap trade check later calls uva_ok, which parses the complete UVA and compares u.user with market.trader.
source_evidence.guards_and_limits: create_market derives the UVA from the canonical trader PDA. Both helpers check the exact fixed executable venue program and event authority. The creator signs as payer. An outsider cannot write arbitrary data at this venue PDA. No current account substitution or funds loss was proved. A changed venue layout could make listing succeed while later trading fails.

items.title: Cashback cleanup depends on external claim instructions
items.description: Unclaimable external cashback can keep deposits blocked after a wipe or the last withdrawal. No current failure of the external claim is proved.

1.evidence: SweepTrader AccountLoaders require canonical config/market/vault, versions, linked trader and trader_wsol; remaining token-leg keys are read from the authenticated market cache and compared at :226-243. A legitimate outstanding cashback balance passes these guards. pump_cashback_claimable:129-135 reads Pump UVA lamports above rent; :248-263 also reads the PumpSwap cashback WSOL ATA and leaves rewards_clear false for a positive balance. Neither account is emptied by this sweep. The trader-source sweep can complete while :334-346 and :371-384 skip VenueRewards. engine::lender::rewards_required:202-208 stays true for a retained pump_uva and every pump venue; deposit delegates to pool::deposit_in:2027-2033, which returns WipeSweepPending without WIPE_REWARDS_CLAIMED. The same dependency covers a wipe, the last-share withdrawal, and retained Pump cashback after migration. A missing or empty cashback account alone does not establish a block.

2.evidence: The reviewed source documents an available permissionless external claim_cashback plus sweep bundle; the trader does not sign. The reports prove no current failed claim, permanent pause, removed interface or reachable malicious external account state. A future external interface change or failure that prevents the claim is the missing state, so the condition is a dependency lead. Referenced prior ELF/runtime tests were not rerun. Later trigger/impact gates are not evaluated.

3.evidence: Stopped after the earlier gate blocker; no later gate was scored.

4.evidence: Stopped after the earlier gate blocker; no later gate was scored.

items.known_issue_comparison: Exact retained dependency in AI2 L76, docs/audit/ai-review-2/triage-venues-2026-10-18.md:64 and prior report:667. That prior issue already describes a donation, a future unavailable trader-signature claim, and WipeSweepPending. AIR2-05/KI-10 explain sweep ownership; AIR2-12 noncanonical cashback routing has a different cause and fix.
items.code_smells: sweep_trader leaves the reward bit clear while external cashback remains; it reads the cashback accounts but cannot empty them.

project_evidence.reason: AI2 L76 already traces a donation into pump UVA/PumpSwap cashback ATA, a future claim-interface change requiring unavailable trader authorization, rewards_clear never becoming true, and WipeSweepPending after wipe or last-lender exit. This is the same retained external-claim dependency. AIR2-12 alternate-destination cashback is a different current-account routing problem and is not a substitute duplicate reason.

source_evidence.trace: rewards_required follows the pump UVA or pump venue. SweepTrader reads the keyed pump UVA and, on PumpSwap, its WSOL ATA. A positive claimable amount leaves rewards_clear false, so the VenueRewards sweep does not set WIPE_REWARDS_CLAIMED. The function never invokes the venue claim itself; callers must bundle the external permissionless claim described by its module. The source asserts current venue claims work without the trader signature. This static pass did not inspect deployed venue bytecode or prove an upgrade that disables those claims. The dependency concerns recovery of outstanding cashback after such a change.

source_evidence.boundary: The trader's authenticated Pump UVA and PumpSwap cashback ATA in sweep_trader's remaining accounts.
source_evidence.proof: With total_shares = 0, wipe_swept = 0, and one claimable cashback unit, rewards_clear is false. sweep_trader sets the trader-swept bit but skips SweepSource::VenueRewards. rewards_required remains true on pump venues and on any market that retains pump_uva. deposit passes that requirement into the math pool, which rejects a missing reward bit with WipeSweepPending. Only an external claim that removes the cashback can enable the next sweep to set the bit.
source_evidence.guards_and_limits: Current documented Pump and PumpSwap claim instructions accept an unsigned trader. The source describes a working external claim plus sweep sequence. This review did not prove a current pause, upgrade, or account state that permanently prevents those claims. This lead concerns the dependency when that external interface stops working. Sweeps constrain every cashback key to the market cache; the caller cannot substitute an empty account.

source_evidence.trace: A wipe or last-share withdrawal clears sweep flags → sweep_trader finds outstanding cashback → the reward bit stays clear → deposit fails WipeSweepPending.
source_evidence.proof: rewards_required returns true for a stored pump UVA or any pump venue. sweep_trader requires the pump UVA's excess lamports to be zero and, on PumpSwap, its cashback WSOL ATA to be empty. The sweep reads those accounts but does not transfer their balances. Its own trader cleanup therefore cannot set WIPE_REWARDS_CLAIMED while external cashback remains. The documented recovery calls pump or PumpSwap claim_cashback before sweep_trader. A program failure that prevents that external claim leaves no clearing path in the reviewed short.win instructions.
source_evidence.guards: Valid external claims are permissionless and can be bundled with the sweep. Missing external accounts normally mean no cashback, so a missing empty account alone does not prove a block. Existing balances remain assigned to the prior lenders; bypassing the bit would transfer their value to later holders. This issue concerns dependence on an unavailable claim, not missing signer authorization.
source_evidence.limitations: No external claim failure or reachable malicious external state was verified. The source comments state that deployed claim paths work; their cited runtime tests were not rerun. This remains a dependency lead, not a proven deposit outage.
source_evidence.fix_direction: Document and validate recovery when the external claim interface changes; preserve the prior holders' cashback entitlement in any fallback.

notes: Any fallback must preserve the prior holders’ cashback entitlement; bypassing the bit can transfer old value to later depositors. All three raw reports remain leads; agreement alone does not supply a currently failing external claim.

items.title: The guard keeps twelve bytes of the ELF hash
items.description: The guard compares twelve hash bytes after ProgramData grows. No practical pair of valid executable files with the same prefix is proved.

1.evidence: The authentic ProgramData address/loader/header checks remain mandatory. After an Emergency revalidation stores a fingerprint, state/venue_guard.rs:48 fixes its size at 12 bytes and elf_fingerprint_of:52-57 copies only that SHA-256 prefix. If the ProgramData length changes and the slot moves, flag_venue_upgraded::is_upgrade:104-107 compares only that prefix of the trimmed ELF. An unchanged-length slot move always counts as an upgrade, independently of the prefix. Thus the conditional collision claim requires a changed account length as well as a matching prefix.

2.evidence: No raw report supplies a valid colliding executable pair or a feasible deployment/search trace. A fixed reviewed fingerprint gives a generic 96-bit second-preimage problem; an actor choosing both executables has a generic 48-bit collision bound, but must still produce deployable ELFs, obtain review of one and control the venue upgrade of the other. Generic work bounds alone do not prove the vulnerable deployed pair. This hardening candidate stops at reachability; later privilege and impact gates are not scored.

3.evidence: Stopped after the earlier gate blocker; no later gate was scored.

4.evidence: Stopped after the earlier gate blocker; no later gate was scored.

KI-69(b) discloses the prefix but its fixed-hash acceptance does not close AIR2-07. This lead is distinct from the empty-fingerprint latch finding.
items.code_smells: elf_fingerprint_of stores only the first twelve SHA-256 bytes; is_upgrade compares that prefix after the account length changes.

project_evidence.reason: AIR2-07 already distinguishes the 96-bit fixed-hash second-preimage cost from the 48-bit generic chosen-pair collision bound of the 12-byte fingerprint. Current guard storage remains 12 bytes. The earlier review also requires changed ProgramData length to suppress a flag; an unchanged-length slot move flags regardless. KI-69 alone is not acceptance of the chosen-pair extension, but AIR2-07 is an exact existing open record.

AIR2-07 already distinguishes the 96-bit fixed-hash second-preimage cost from the 48-bit generic chosen-pair collision bound of the 12-byte fingerprint. Current guard storage remains 12 bytes. The earlier review also requires changed ProgramData length to suppress a flag; an unchanged-length slot move flags regardless. KI-69 alone is not acceptance of the chosen-pair extension, but AIR2-07 is an exact existing open record.

source_evidence.trace: GUARD_ELF_LEN=12 yields a 96-bit stored fingerprint. A venue authority that chooses both ELFs can seek a pair with the same prefix, obtain review of one, then extend and replace it with the other. The generic chosen-pair work is about 2^48 hashes; this review supplies no collision, practical search budget, or usable malicious ELF pair. The full 32-byte reviewed hash is present at revalidation but not retained.

source_evidence.boundary: The fingerprint used to distinguish a ProgramData extension from an upgrade after the account grows.
source_evidence.proof: GUARD_ELF_LEN is 12. elf_fingerprint_of iterates over that 12-byte destination, so bytes 12 through 31 never participate in the later comparison.
source_evidence.guards_and_limits: A fixed reviewed fingerprint requires a generic 96-bit second-preimage search. An actor who chooses both executable versions has a generic 48-bit collision bound. The attacker also needs a valid deployable executable, authority to upgrade the venue, and an account-length change. No colliding pair or present exploit was constructed. This is separate from the proven empty-fingerprint path.

notes: A full-digest change requires an explicit versioned guard-layout migration with coordinated clients; no migration patch was supplied by these raws.

items.title: The base mint reader omits account type checks
items.description: A future caller without a trusted mint key can read token-account bytes as mint supply. Current caller keys block that substitution.

1.evidence: mint::read_base:169-176 checks one of the two token owners and length >=82, then base_of verifies COption tags and initialized==1. A constructed 165-byte buffer with byte 45=1 and zero option tags passes despite the legacy mint length; a Token-2022 buffer with the same base and account type 2 at offset 165 also passes. This is a parser counterexample, not a proved token-owned runtime account at a permitted key. PumpSwap check_read:401-412 binds its LP account to the real pool.lp_mint; pool parse failure prevents its use. Keeper mint_supply:187-191 receives stored-market mint accounts. Listing check_mint_safety establishes the market mint and stronger mint::check rejects incorrect shapes; Raydium lp_supply additionally requires Tokenkeg and exactly 82 bytes. Owner/write rules prevent fabricating different bytes at these trusted keys. No current unprivileged substitution passes these guards; retain hardening and stop.

L38 hardening added exact mint length to Raydium’s LP helper, not to this shared reader or PumpSwap’s caller. The new buffer illustration does not establish a new reachable substitution path.

project_evidence.reason: The original venue-state report names read_base itself, minimum length without SPL exact-length/Token-2022 type checks, crafted token-account bytes, and constrained current caller keys. L38 subsequently hardened the Raydium LP helper, not this generic base reader. The candidate repeats that exact remaining helper-boundary hardening mechanism.

source_evidence.proof: For a 165-byte buffer under TOKEN_PROGRAM, set byte 45 to 1 and leave COption tags at 0 and 46 equal to zero. read_base returns Ok even though SPL mints have exactly 82 bytes. A Token-2022 buffer with the same prefix and account type 2 at offset 165 also passes. The stronger mint::check rejects both shapes. The linked spl-token-2022-interface 2.1.0 StateWithExtensions::<Mint>::unpack checks length, padding, and AccountType::Mint.
source_evidence.path: pump_amm::lp_mint_supply at programs/shortwin/src/venues/pump_amm.rs:419 and keeper::mint_supply at services/keeper/src/view.rs:187 call this weaker reader. PumpSwap's LP key comes from its real pool, and keeper mint keys come from stored markets.
source_evidence.guards: The reader verifies program owner, minimum length, valid COption tags, and initialized byte 1. Listing uses check_mint_safety. Raydium's lp_supply additionally requires Tokenkeg and exactly 82 bytes. Stored market and pool keys prevent caller-selected token-account substitution today.
source_evidence.impact: The library contract permits a wrong account type. A future unbound call could interpret unrelated bytes as fee-tier supply.
source_evidence.limitations: No current unprivileged path to substitute a different account at the trusted mint keys was proved. This remains a hardening lead.

items.title: The Raydium readers omit vault authority checks
items.description: The live readers omit vault authority checks. A future venue-authorized change can leave accepted reserves unusable; no current public authority-change path is proved.

Token decoding also checks account type, initialization and COption tags. An outsider cannot mutate the venue PDA’s token authority or substitute another key. No present external instruction that creates the proposed authority transition was established; the claimed future state is retained only as hardening and later gates stop.

items.title: Normal curve quotes use the original mint supply
items.description: Normal curve quotes can choose a different fee after a burn under multiple tiers. The documented single-tier schedule prevents this today.

1.evidence: fees::pump_curve:164-165 passes PUMP_CURVE_MCAP_SUPPLY=10^15 to curve_fees_at, which computes floor(vq*supply/vt) and selects the tier. With vt=300e12, vq=100e9 and live supply=600e12, fixed/live market caps are 333333333333/200000000000 lamports; a hypothetical 250e9 threshold separates them. The raw integer example gives net=334448162 for q=10^12 and costs 337792644/338628765 at 100/125 bps, a difference of 836121. This is arithmetic evidence only. pump_curve::pricing_inputs:454 and :481 use the ordinary fixed resolver even though :470-472 separately resolves synthetic fees at live supply; quote::curve_synthetic keeps ordinary fees for q<=rt, so the synthetic correction does not change the ordinary branch.

2.evidence: fees.rs:45-50 expressly states that the reviewed curve schedule has one flat tier at zero; any supply therefore selects that same tier. External fee data is constrained by key, owner and discriminator, so a caller cannot substitute the hypothetical multi-tier schedule. No live account read or active multi-tier deployment was established. A future authenticated schedule change is required; no wrong present quote is proved, and the hardening label remains a lead. Later gates are not evaluated.

items.known_issue_comparison: Exact fixed-basis part of accepted KI-77(b), earlier math/venue reports and pass-1 shortwin-math|pump-curve|hardening-fixed-supply-fee-basis. KI-77 explicitly retains ordinary quotes up to rT, sales and fee gates on 10^15 while synthetic fees use live supply. This library function stays separate from adapter pricing_inputs and ordinary spot-risk-fee policy; NEW in the initial ledger was not project-new.
items.code_smells: pump_curve uses PUMP_CURVE_MCAP_SUPPLY for ordinary fees; only the separate synthetic resolver receives the live supply.

project_evidence.reason: The original math and venue reports already record fixed 10^15 supply for ordinary curve fees against live-supply venue fees after burns under hypothetical multiple tiers. KI-77 retains this ordinary basis while adding separate live-supply synthetic fees. This is the same mechanism as p1-a01-b01, with a different entry point, not project-new merely because the new ledger starts empty.

source_evidence.path: A token holder burns circulating tokens → a future multi-tier schedule separates the fixed and live market caps → pump_curve selects the fixed-supply tier → normal curve quotes use that fee.
source_evidence.proof: fees.rs defines PUMP_CURVE_MCAP_SUPPLY = 1_000_000_000_000_000 and passes it to curve_fees_at. That helper computes floor(vq * supply / vt), then selects the last tier whose threshold is at most the result. For vt = 300_000_000_000_000, vq = 100_000_000_000, and live supply = 600_000_000_000_000, the fixed market cap is 333_333_333_333 lamports and the live market cap is 200_000_000_000. A hypothetical threshold of 250_000_000_000 separates them. If the lower tier has a 125 bps protocol fee and the higher tier has 100 bps, the normal resolver returns 100 bps while the live-supply resolver returns 125 bps. For q = 1_000_000_000_000, the normal curve quote has net = ceil(q * vq / (vt - q)) + 1 = 334_448_162. Its cost is 337_792_644 at 100 bps and 338_628_765 at 125 bps, a difference of 836_121 lamports. This is a pure integer calculation, not execution evidence.
source_evidence.caller_evidence: pricing_inputs receives supply but calls fees::pump_curve for its ordinary fees and its EMA fee. It separately calls pump_curve_at_supply for synthetic_fees. curve_synthetic retains ordinary curve_fees when q <= state.rt. Thus the existing synthetic correction does not change the ordinary branch.
source_evidence.guards_and_limitations: fees.rs:46-52 explicitly states that the current curve schedule has one tier at threshold zero. That condition makes the two market-cap bases select the same tier today. Owner-checked external fee data controls the schedule. This review did not inspect live accounts or prove an active multi-tier deployment. The open's min_notional, margin and fee gates do not select the missing supply basis, but they do prevent tiny notional and insufficient margin inputs. A trade CPI can reject an inadequate maximum input. This item remains a hardening lead, not an active exploit finding.
source_evidence.impact: A future fee threshold can cause a normal quote to differ from the venue charge after a burn. The difference can affect trade bounds and risk values that use that quote.
source_evidence.related_scope: The adapter call is supporting evidence for this shared-library cause. This block does not assert a separate synthetic-fee gate defect.

notes: A trade CPI can reject inadequate maximum input, and min_notional/margin/fee gates still apply. These bounds do not supply the missing live fee schedule or convert the hypothetical calculation into an active exploit.

1.evidence: Accounts first: FlagVenueUpgraded:50-67 requires the canonical AccountLoader VenueGuard PDA/version, a venue index below VENUE_PROGRAMS, the compiled ProgramData key and loader owner; read_deploy_slot also requires its ProgramData header. Real CPMM ProgramData passes; there is no trusted signer. Local loader 4.2.2:793-794 and 4.3.0:789-790 dispatch legacy ExtendProgram with check_authority=false. Both require matching writable Program/ProgramData, loader ownership, a positive permitted increase, an upgradeable authority field, a later slot and rent funding; an outsider can supply these without the upgrade authority signature. Both resize, redeploy the unchanged ELF and store clock_slot. With guard_slot[4]=100, upgraded=0, guard_len[2]=0 and a successful extension in slot 101, flag_venue_upgraded:128 passes and :130-135 skips is_upgrade because VenueGuard::elf_fingerprint:110-114 returns None; :136 sets bit 4. Ordinary init/revalidation and downstream guards are traced below, not bypassed.

2.evidence: Source-reachable but deployment-conditional: InitializeConfig requires the real short.win upgrade-authority signer and new canonical accounts; an honest init writes upgraded=0 and guard_slot at :156-160 while leaving all fingerprint lengths zero. The enabled-venue bitmask permits CPMM. RevalidateVenue requires the configured pause-authority signer, canonical config/guard and authentic ProgramData; at the current expected_slot it accepts expected_elf_hash=[0;32], clears the fingerprint and clears the latch (:72-108). Neither path requires malicious governance. The outsider extension additionally requires a still-upgradeable account below the 10 MiB cap and a compatible active loader. Use 10,240 bytes when available, or the permitted smaller final increase to the cap. Immutable/full-sized accounts block this path; source-described capped Pump/PumpSwap accounts are excluded. No live fingerprint, size, authority or feature-state query was performed; source comments identifying growable venues are not live deployment validation.

3.evidence: The outsider pays any extension rent shortfall and transaction fees, then sends flag_venue_upgraded with authentic accounts. The matching account/address and payer signature requirements do not require the venue upgrade signer or the short.win Emergency signer. Honest init creates the condition directly, so this is an unprivileged amplifier of an ordinary initialization state, not harm caused solely by a malicious admin.

4.evidence: For an otherwise eligible existing Raydium market, open_short:291 calls guard::latch, whose :110-115 rejects the set bit before the trade. GUARD_MASK_RAYDIUM contains both Raydium bits, so either Raydium open is refused. The actual borrower signer, canonical config/guard/market, linked mint/vault/trader and usual prologue checks can all be satisfied by an honest caller; they do not clear the latch. create_market:553 also checks this Raydium mask; propose_pool:240 uses candidate_latch and blocks the flagged candidate program; execute_pool_switch:208 treats a flagged candidate as inadmissible. Existing exits, add_margin and withdrawals do not consult this latch; no existing funds lock or attacker profit is proved. The static complete conditional path scores 100 - 15 bounded/recoverable interruption - 10 specific hashless, still-growable state = 75. No runtime execution is claimed.

1.evidence: The authentic ProgramData address/loader/header checks remain mandatory. After an Emergency revalidation stores a fingerprint, state/venue_guard.rs:48 fixes its size at 12 bytes and elf_fingerprint_of:52-57 copies only that SHA-256 prefix. If the ProgramData length changes and the slot moves, flag_venue_upgraded::is_upgrade:104-107 compares only that prefix of the trimmed ELF. 2.evidence: No raw report supplies a valid colliding executable pair or a feasible deployment/search trace.
